Anal. sacra, V2, 282-283, qui diversam in idem argumentum scriptionem edidit.
Codex Mediolan. 23, f. 250 (Catal. Astrol., p. 15) fragmentum ex alio simili sed
ampliore tractatu complectitur, cui praefigitur nomen Alexandri regis, ubi
multa sunt quae cum cod. Neapol. consentiunt. Exempli gratia ea afferemus quae
de herba solis dicuntur :
Δευτέρα βοτάνη Ἡλίου πολύγονος. αὕτη εἴληφε τὴν προσωνυμίαν ἐξ οὗ
τὸν Ἥλιον πᾶσιν [cod. πάσης] ἀρχηγὸν <εἶναι> νενόμισται· ταύτην δέ τινες
χαμαιλέοντα προσηγόρευσαν, ὅ ἐστι οἶκος Ἡλίου. αὕτη πινομένη [cod. τινο-
μένη] θεραπεύει τὰ περὶ τὸ στῆθος καὶ στομαχικὰ πάθη, καθάπερ καὶ τὸ ζῴδιον τὰ
μέρη λέλαχεν. ἐνεργεῖ δὲ καὶ συμπαθῶς ἡ βοτάνη διὰ τὸ ὄνομα [an διὰ τοῦ ὀνόμα-
τος?]· πινόμενος δὲ ὁ χυλὸς αὐτῆς ἑτοιμοτέρους πρὸς γονὴν καὶ ἀφροδίσια καθί-
στησι, περιαφθεῖσα δὲ ἡ ῥίζα ὀφθαλμιῶντας [cod. ὀφθαλμῶντας] ἀπαλλάσσει, εἰ
δέ τις πρὸ τοῦ πάσχειν περιαφθείη, οὐκ ἐᾷ ἐπὶ τὸ σύνολον ὀφθαλμιᾶσαι. ἁρμόζει
δὲ καὶ τοῖς φρενιτικοῖς καὶ ληθαργικοῖς περιαπτομένη, καθότι τὸν περὶ καρδίας
τόπον ὁ Ἥλιος ἔλαχε<ν>· εὔπνοιαν <δὲ> παρέχει καὶ τοῖς πνευμονιῶσιν ὡς ἐπὶ
τῶν γενέσεων· ἐπὶ δὲ πρώτους ἐν ἡμῖν φρενιτικοὺς καὶ ληθαργικοὺς ... νομίζων δὲ
† ἀφένα καθίστησι· ποιεῖ δὲ καὶ πρὸς ῥοὴν γυναικεῖον προποτιζομένη τῷ χυλῷ.
sections.en: Anal. sacra, V2, 282-283, who published a different writing on the same subject. Codex Mediolan. 23, f. 250 (Catal. Astrol., p. 15) contains a fragment from another similar but larger treatise, to which the name of King Alexander is prefixed, where there are many things which agree with cod. Neapol. For example, we will adduce those things which are said about the herb of the sun: The second plant of the Sun is polygonos. This has received the appellation from the fact that the Sun is considered to be the leader of all [cod. of all (fem.)]; and some have called this chamaileon, which is the house of the Sun. This, when drunk [cod. when punished], cures the affections around the chest and stomach, just as the zodiac sign has obtained the parts. And the plant acts also sympathetically through the name [or through the name?]; and the juice of it, when drunk, makes them readier for offspring and sexual intercourse, and the root, when tied around, relieves those suffering from ophthalmia [cod. those suffering from ophthalmia], and if someone should tie it around before suffering, it does not allow them to suffer from ophthalmia at all. And it is suitable also for the frenzied and the lethargic when tied around, inasmuch as the Sun has obtained the place around the heart; and it provides good breathing also to those suffering from pneumonia as in the case of nativities; and for the first among us frenzied and lethargic ... and considering † ... it establishes; and it acts also for the flow of women when given to drink beforehand with the juice.

summary.headline: Planetary Herbs and Remedies
summary.text: Astrological herbal correspondences continue with plants of Aphrodite, Hermes, Ares, and Zeus, detailing remedies for ophthalmia, sexual ailments, hemorrhoids, joint and spleen disorders, dysuria, dysentery, and evil demons. A note compares Codex Mediolanensis 23 and a larger treatise attributed to King Alexander, quoting the Sun’s herb, polygonos.
